page: Amazon Web Services r9gd.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated physical cores using the custom 64-bit ARM architecture developed by AWS. The processors operate at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, ensuring dedicated compute resources without hyperthreading.

The instance is equipped with 1536.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. For local storage, the server includes 11400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. This combination of high-capacity memory and fast local storage is designed for data-intensive workloads, though the ephemeral nature of instance store volumes requires external replication strategies for data persistence.

Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture provides a high density of physical cores and memory relative to traditional x86 architectures, which can lower operational overhead for compatible software ecosystems. However, workloads must be compiled for ARM64 to run on this platform, representing a potential migration tradeoff.

The hardware configuration makes this instance suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, big data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that benefit from high-speed local NVMe storage and high-throughput networking.
